name: Treaty with the Wyandot, etc., 1818
aka: Supplementary Treaty of St. Mary's, September 17, 1818
nations: Seneca of Sandusky and of Lewistown (Seneca-Cayuga Nation)
Shawnee of Wapakoneta, Hog Creek and Lewistown (Shawnee Tribe, Eastern Shawnee Tribe)
Odawa (Ottawa) of the Maumee and Blanchard's Fork (Ottawa Tribe of Oklahoma)
promises: Article 1: the tracts the 1817 Fort Meigs treaty would have granted to chiefs in fee were instead excepted from the cession and reserved for the use of the listed Indians and their heirs forever, unless ceded to the United States.

Article 2: added reserves: 55,680 acres for the Wyandot, 16,000 acres at Big Spring and 160 acres on the Sandusky for Wyandot at Solomon's town and Blanchard's Fork, 12,800 acres for the Shawnee at Wapakoneta, 8,960 acres for the Shawnee and Seneca at Lewistown, and 10,000 acres for the Seneca on the Sandusky.
Article 4: additional perpetual annuities: $500 to the Wyandot, $1,000 to the Shawnee and Seneca of Lewistown, $500 to the Seneca and $1,500 to the Ottawa.

breaches.what: Treating this treaty and the 1817 treaty it supplemented as one cession effective January 4, 1819, the Commission found Royce Areas 87 and 88 were worth $5,698,821.60 ($1.20 an acre), that the $220,000 in consideration under the two treaties was unconscionable, and awarded net sums to the Wyandot, Ottawa, Delaware, Shawnee, Chippewa and Potawatomi plaintiffs.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Indian Claims Commission, Strong et al. v. United States, Dockets 13-F, 15-I, 27, 29-G, 64-A, 133-C, 141 and 308, Interlocutory Order, 43 Ind. Cl. Comm. 311

source.title: Strong et al. v. United States, Docket 13-F et al., Interlocutory Order (September 22, 1978)
source.publisher: Oklahoma State University Library, Indian Claims Commission Decisions

compensation: Net sums ordered on September 22, 1978, less any gratuitous offsets: Wyandot $2,348,679.60; Ottawa $1,692,028.56; Delaware $487,235.92; Shawnee $437,735.92; Chippewa $258,820.80; Potawatomi $254,320.80. Final award and payment were not traced.
today: The Commission's 1973 title decision in these dockets (30 Ind. Cl. Comm. 337) held that six tribes held recognized title to Areas 87 and 88 in undivided shares; the 1978 opinion reports it was affirmed by the Court of Claims (207 Ct. Cl. 959, 1975) and certiorari was denied (423 U.S. 903, 1976). The Commission read Article 4 as a single $1,000 annuity shared by the Shawnee and the Seneca of Lewistown, not $1,000 each.

openQuestions: The map draws this entry with the reserve cessions listed in treaties.json (Royce 163, 164, 165, 171, 211, 213, 259); the Commission's finding concerns Areas 87 and 88, the land ceded under the 1817 and 1818 treaties together.

The 1978 interlocutory order cites the treaty as "7 Stat. 179"; the opinion of the same day and the treaty text give 7 Stat. 178. The opinion text also reads $5,698,833.60 where the order reads $5,698,821.60; the order is used.
Whether the perpetual annuities of Article 4 were paid, commuted or ended, and how the Article 1 and 2 reserves were later ceded, was not researched here.
